wiring_location: briefing.py::_mx_ok() (around line 1152-1173), called from ai_briefs()'s real Gemini-based production path -- NOT mx_note(), which is only the fallback used when it["mx"] is absent
wiring_method: minimal insertion -- no rewrite of _mx_ok()'s existing checks (brief/point length, MX_BAN, _mx_copied all unchanged)
scope_implemented: Only the documented causal/attribution marker check (metaxis_point_grounding._has_causal_claim) is enforced in production. A causal/attribution-phrased Point with no source_document_evidence/evidence_network_refs/intelligence_object_refs (always the case today, since briefing.py items carry no per-item evidence/claim/intelligence ids) is downgraded: the Point ("p") is dropped to an empty string, the QUICK BRIEF ("b") is kept.
scope_not_implemented: Full SOURCE_SUPPORTED / EVIDENCE_NETWORK_SUPPORTED / INTELLIGENCE_OBJECT_SUPPORTED grounding for every non-causal Point is NOT wired -- briefing.py's items have no evidence_ids/claim_ids/intelligence_ids fields yet, so applying the module's strict default (ungrounded-and-non-causal = UNSUPPORTED_INTERPRETATION) in production would drop nearly all Points and is an unacceptable regression. This is an honest, deliberate scope limit, not an oversight.
failure_mode: wrapped in try/except -- any grounding-module load/call failure is swallowed and the pre-N-1 behavior (Point kept as-is) is preserved, so this wiring can never crash or regress the existing pipeline
status_reason: The literal banned example from Te's spec (causal/attribution AI-demand claims with no evidence) is now blocked in the real production path. General non-causal unsupported-interpretation blocking remains a known gap pending per-item evidence/claim/intelligence-object wiring in a future phase.
